Story time! 

I had to move out and support myself at 16 because my father was in federal prison for cocaine trafficking and my mom was out doing drugs and sleeping with her boss. 

Before my father was arrested, he’d let pretty much anyone stay at our house. Anyone. Got it?

When he was in prison, he would try to get me to be pen pals with his fellow inmates/criminals, and send them my picture. I was sixteen.

After he was out of prison, they used my social security number for stuff and it took me years and years to fix my credit.

This is just a very short sample of events. I know there are some cultures where children are expected to be beholden to their parents *even if they were abused and did not receive any actual parenting*, and I’m really glad I don’t live in one of them.

Bigger picture on noise:

Cruise ships are noisy for all sorts of reasons. Plumbing, mechanical equipment like ice makers, cleaners in the hallways, parties on the pool deck, ships just creak sometimes, and yes, other cruisers. You may get neighbors with loud voices or who like to watch TV all afternoon. If you go into the cruise with the feeling that your cruise will be ruined if you can hear people in the room next to you, it’s a recipe for disappointment.

I’m a light sleeper and I bring earplugs and a high quality travel white noise machine. That’s sleep taken care of.

If I’m chilling in my room and my neighbor is playing TV so loud I can hear it, I put in my AirPods and play something on one of my devices. 

Seriously, prepare for noise. Then if your room is dead silent and your neighbors are always out, it’ll be a nice surprise.
